plan.summary: This 1-4 block fits the first quarter of a 12-week off-camp build for boxing with only one S&C session each week and bodyweight-only equipment. Week 1 establishes simple baselines with a lower-body strength assessment using a hard split squat set, then Weeks 2-4 build general force, low-impact power, trunk strength, and conditioning without creating too much soreness for boxing practice. Because your goal leans toward strength, power, and endurance with more conditioning, each session keeps the main strength work first and finishes with practical bodyweight conditioning. Week 1 is for establishing training maxes on the primary lift style used in this block, and the main progression starts in Week 2.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic unilateral leg strength, low-impact jump power, trunk strength, and aerobic-repeatability with simple bodyweight work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the same movement patterns with harder variations and slightly denser conditioning while keeping technique clean.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and shift more emphasis to crisp power, fast contacts, and boxing-friendly conditioning output.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Stick the landing softly and jump as high and fast as you can on every rep. Rest enough to keep each jump sharp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement makes timing messy. Start from a still quarter squat and jump cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if jump landings feel clumsy. Keep contacts light and springy.

exercises.name: 1b. Plyometric Push-Up from Knees
exercises.notes: Explode off the floor with a straight body line. If you cannot leave the floor cleanly, make it a fast push-up instead.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a bench, sofa, or sturdy surface if floor speed work is too hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Standard Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you can move well but cannot yet produce air time.

exercises.name: 2. Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with easier bodyweight split squats, then build to one hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side using a backpack or slow tempo if needed. This sets your baseline for future lower-body strength work. Stop if balance or knee control breaks.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log the hardest clean set on each side with the variation used so you can compare progress later.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to one hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side. Use load, tempo, or range of motion to make it challenging and log the exact variation.

substitutionOptions.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot elevation setup is awkward. Keep the front foot fully planted and use a full range.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if balance is the main limiter. Make it hard with a slow lowering phase and a full pause at the bottom.

exercises.name: 3. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a variation you can perform with 1-2 clean reps left in reserve. Body stays rigid and chest reaches full depth.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups are not yet clean at the target reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if normal push-ups are too easy.

exercises.name: 4. Side Plank
exercises.notes: Keep ribs down, glutes tight, and the body in one straight line. Do not let the top shoulder roll forward.

substitutionOptions.name: Long-Lever Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the standard version is too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Bent-Knee Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full version is too demanding.

exercises.name: 5. Bodyweight Aerobic Circuit
exercises.notes: Keep the pace steady and nasal breathing if possible. This should build work capacity, not turn into a sloppy max-effort session.

endurancePrescription.target: Whole-body work capacity with extra trunk and shoulder endurance for boxing
endurancePrescription.notes: Rotate through marching in place, mountain climbers, fast shadowboxing, reverse lunges, and plank shoulder taps.

circuitPrescription.targetAreaEmphasis: Roughly 60% whole-body aerobic work, 25% trunk and shoulder endurance, 15% leg repeatability
circuitPrescription.progression: In later weeks, add one round or slightly increase station difficulty before making the rest shorter.
circuitPrescription.analytics: Track whether you complete all stations at a steady pace with clean movement and controlled breathing.

substitutionOptions.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat

exercises.name: 3. Push-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up

exercises.name: 4. Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Lower back stays gently pressed down and ribs stay tucked. Shorten the lever if your low back lifts.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold is too hard to keep clean.

substitutionOptions.name: V-Sit Tuck Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a harder trunk challenge without extra equipment.

exercises.name: 5. Shadowboxing Tempo Intervals
exercises.notes: Keep the rounds smooth and technical. Focus on rhythm, posture, and breathing while holding a steady work rate.

endurancePrescription.notes: Use simple combinations, active feet, and relaxed shoulders.
